section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes validation of the Persian BAS-2 in an Iranian university sample, reporting a one-factor structure and internal consistency in men and women, with item 10 showing low loading in females. The BAS-2 correlated positively (small magnitude) with self-esteem and life satisfaction, showed a negative association with BMI in women and a positive association with BMI/BMI2 in men, and had a small positive association with age; BMI was self-reported and the sample was university-based. The authors note limitations including university-only sampling, self-reported BMI, and lack of ethnicity data, and recommend further cross-cultural validation.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a psychometric evaluation of the Persian BAS-2 in an Iranian university (college) sample, finding a one-factor structure and internal consistency across men and women. Convergent validity evidence was small: BAS-2 correlated positively with self-esteem and life satisfaction; BAS-2 was negatively associated with BMI in women (r = −.24) but positively associated with BMI in men (r = .12); age showed a small positive relationship with body appreciation. Limitations noted include the university-only sample, self-reported BMI, and lack of ethnicity data.
